h1: Irene Resort Koh Lipe — Pool Villas Where You Step From Bed to Sea on Sunrise Beach
intro: Picture this: you wake on the island people call "Thailand's Maldives," slide back a wall of floor-to-ceiling glass to find turquoise Andaman sea in front of you, drop into your own pool whose edge meets the sand, and a floating breakfast glides over to you — this is Irene Resort Koh Lipe, one of the few genuinely luxury stays set right on Sunrise Beach · 16 private-pool villas built for seclusion, holder of a 2025 MICHELIN Key · from approx ฿14,500/night for a standard villa.
galleryAlts: Irene Resort's large infinity pool with swim-up bar and sun loungers facing the sea
Sunrise Beach in front of the resort with fine white sand, clear water and a beach sala
A floating breakfast tray drifting in a villa's private plunge pool

body.html: Koh Lipe has plenty of places to sleep, but you can count the genuine 5-star stays on one hand · Irene arrived as a pool-villa resort pitched a notch above the rest of the island — 16 standalone villas, every one with its own pool, high walls for privacy and floor-to-ceiling glass framing either sea or treetops · In 2025 it earned a MICHELIN Key, which on a small island like this is a rare badge to carry.

Villas come in three flavours · Tree Pool Villa (138 sqm) sits up on the slope among the trees with resort-and-distant-sea views and the friendliest price — a few steps from the beach · Sand Beachfront Pool Villa (110 sqm) is the Maldives-style detached villa right on the sand, open the door and you're on the beach · Sun Beachfront Pool Villa (118 sqm) is the same idea on the very front row, its pool fitted with a glass side panel so you see the sea while you swim, and the highest price · Several reviewers question whether Sun's premium over Sand is worth it, given most guests are out exploring the islands by morning.
"Lying in my own pool in the morning, sea right in front with nothing in the way, then the breakfast tray floats over — that moment alone felt worth it."

The hero of the shared space is an infinity pool many guests call the biggest on Koh Lipe, with a built-in jacuzzi, loungers, umbrellas and a swim-up bar · The edge looks straight out over Sunrise Beach · This stretch of beach has clear, swim-friendly water and gentle waves, with fewer longtail boats moored than other sides — which keeps the mornings quiet and perfect for a floating breakfast.

On the food, Bok e'tto serves Mediterranean-Asian dishes right on the beach with your toes in the sand — dinner here comes up often in reviews · Breakfast is a set menu brought to your table, which some love for the hot, fresh dishes while others wish for an à la carte choice · Where Irene stands out is the extras: floating breakfast in your pool, beach picnics, and private longtail boat tours around the islands.

The location is on a quieter stretch of Sunrise Beach — about an 8-minute walk to Walking Street, the island's central lane with restaurants, mini-marts and tour desks · One honest note from reviews: the main entrance via the back of the resort is a sandy road that feels a little plain, not the grand arrival you might imagine, though the mood changes the moment you're inside · In late 2025–early 2026 there was construction on an expansion, and some reviews mention dust and noise — worth checking the status with the resort before you book.

Honestly, Irene is not a stay for every budget · Villa rates swing hard by season, from around ฿14,000 in normal periods up to ฿22,000+ at peak, and Koh Lipe is an island where many places close in low season (May–October) for the monsoon · If your trip is all-day snorkelling and you'll barely be in the room, this spend may not pay off · But if you want the stay to be part of the trip — your own pool by the sea, real privacy, attentive service — Irene delivers at a level that's hard to find on this island.

A tip from reading the real reviews: on a tighter budget, the Tree Pool Villa is the best value — you still get a private pool and the largest footprint of the three, in exchange for a slightly longer walk to the sand · If you want to fall asleep to the waves and step straight onto the beach, Sand is plenty; you don't need to upgrade to Sun · And ask whether the floating breakfast is included in your package, as it's sometimes thrown in.

highlights.title: Biggest infinity pool on the island
highlights.text: A large central pool with a built-in jacuzzi and swim-up bar looking straight out over Sunrise Beach — many reviews rate it the best pool on Koh Lipe.

highlights.title: 16 private-pool villas
highlights.text: Every villa has its own pool, floor-to-ceiling glass framing sea or treetops, Maldives-style design, and beachfront options where you step from bed to sand.

highlights.title: Bok e'tto + floating breakfast
highlights.text: Beachfront Mediterranean-Asian dining with your toes in the sand, plus a floating breakfast in your private pool that many guests come specifically for.

honestSummary: Irene Resort Koh Lipe is one of the few luxury stays on Koh Lipe that genuinely puts pool villas on Sunrise Beach, with the biggest infinity pool on the island · It's a fine fit for couples, honeymooners, or anyone who wants the stay to be part of the trip · But you have to accept the high, season-swinging rates — and whether the top villa category is worth it remains debatable.
honestChecks: If you'll be out snorkelling and island-hopping all day — the private pool and luxury villa go barely used and won't pay off → pick a well-located, lower-priced stay on the island.
If you're budget-conscious but still want a private pool — skip the Sun Beachfront and choose the Tree Pool Villa or Sand → you get a very similar experience for several thousand baht less.
If you're planning a low-season trip (May–Oct) — Koh Lipe's monsoon closes many places and cuts ferry runs → confirm the resort is open and check the expansion-works status before booking.

tips.title: On a budget, pick the Tree Pool Villa
tips.body: The Tree Pool Villa is the friendliest price yet has the largest footprint (138 sqm) and its own pool — in exchange for a slightly longer walk to the sand.

tips.title: Ask about the floating breakfast
tips.body: The resort sometimes includes a floating breakfast in the package — check before booking; if not included you can add it. It photographs beautifully and is a highlight for many.

tips.title: Book the private boat tour ahead
tips.body: Private longtail tours around Lipe-Adang can be arranged through the resort; high season fills fast, so book ahead to catch the calm early-morning sea.

tips.title: Avoid low season, check status first
tips.body: Koh Lipe's rainy season (May–Oct) brings strong monsoon; many places close and ferries thin out. Best window is Nov–Apr · If works are ongoing, request a villa away from that zone.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Irene Resort Koh Lipe

faq.q: Which beach is Irene Resort Koh Lipe on, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It sits right on Sunrise Beach, Koh Lipe, in Satun Province · It's about an 8-minute walk to the island's central Walking Street · To reach Koh Lipe you take a ferry from Pak Bara pier (Satun) or a nearby province, then transfer by longtail boat onto the beach. The resort offers a pier transfer — arrange it in advance.

faq.q: What does Irene Resort cost, and what villa types are there?
faq.a: From approx ฿14,500/night for the Tree Pool Villa (138 sqm, with a private pool) · The Sand Beachfront Pool Villa on the sand is around ฿16,500 · The front-row Sun Beachfront Pool Villa runs ฿22,000+ · Rates swing significantly by season and climb fast at peak, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Irene Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for couples, honeymooners, and anyone who wants the stay to be part of the trip · Every villa has a private pool, with a focus on seclusion and a beachfront mood · If you'll be out snorkelling all day and barely in the room, a well-located, lower-priced stay may offer better value.

faq.q: What is Irene's stretch of Sunrise Beach like — can you swim?
faq.a: Sunrise Beach has fine white sand, clear water and gentle waves you can swim in · The stretch in front of the resort has fewer moored longtail boats than other spots, so mornings are quiet and ideal for a floating breakfast — and it's one of the best sunrise-viewing spots on the island.

faq.q: When should you visit Irene Resort, and is there construction?
faq.a: The best window is November–April, with calm seas and clear skies · The rainy season (May–Oct) brings strong monsoon, many island closures and reduced ferry runs · In late 2025–early 2026 there was expansion construction and some reviews mention dust and noise — check the status with the resort and request a villa away from the works zone before booking.

faq.q: Is Irene Resort the same as Irene Pool Villa Resort?
faq.a: They're the same brand on Sunrise Beach · Irene Pool Villa Resort is the original 16-villa section, while Irene Resort (Phase 2) is the newer beachfront-room expansion · The two sit side by side and share facilities such as the central pool, restaurant and spa · When booking, match the room/villa name to exactly what you want.
